Another three hours pass like this. The sun puts itself in an unpleasant position as it starts to creep downward, right in their eyes as they drive west. When they return to civilization, Mydei makes Phainon take over again, stretching a bit before he settles into the passenger seat, loading up a couple of the songs he’d wanted to make Phainon play before the lack of data cut him off.

This first one has a full minute of electric guitar for an intro, and Phainon gets all excited saying he should learn it.

“I play acoustic, Phainon,” Mydei reminds him, but he just grumbles a bit and gets excited again as soon as the vocalist comes in.

“You could sing too!” he says. “You’ve got that growl like he does, you totally could!” He glances at Mydei, bug eyed with the sunglasses and smiling enough for Mydei to see the points of his teeth, and Mydei can’t do anything but laugh in his face, incredulous.

“Absolutely fucking not.”

It takes about forty-five minutes, but the road they take gradually turns windy and steep as they disappear from the city and into a mountain range that blocks out the sun. It’s verdant and lush this time of year, and in the shade it’s almost cool, so they roll down their windows to breathe the air. Phainon takes the sunglasses off and looks like a happy dog with the wind in his hair. Mydei watches his profile. The line of his nose, his jaw, the choker around his throat. His gaze is sticky. He turns away before he can get stuck.

The car grumbles as it climbs the slope, Phainon on the gas, not speeding much on a road that curves this much. Give him a straight-away and he’ll go thirty over the speed limit without even noticing it, give him bends and turns and hills and he’ll end up ten under and white-knuckled on the steering wheel. At the very least, Mydei’s never felt unsafe with him at the wheel.

“Thank god we’re in my car and not yours,” he says as they reach the crest of the hill. The road evens out for a quarter mile or so before another incline starts. Around them, trees whisk by and wind buffets them from the open windows.

“Mine would make it,” Phainon protests, barely sparing a glance as the road starts to curve a bit. His fingers clench tight on the steering wheel. 

A sign: SCENIC OVERLOOK 2 MILES. Mydei props an elbow on the window and fights the smile that tries to creep its way onto his lips. “Respectfully, Phainon,” he says, “you drive a fucking canoe.”

“Shut up, it’s not a canoe,” Phainon complains, bouncing his free leg and saying the word canoe all silly.

He drives a 1999 Toyota Avalon. Peeling off-white paint, three rock chips in the windshield, an interior that smells faintly like gasoline. It’s low to the ground, short, and looks, frankly, like a fucking canoe. He bought it off a neighbor and is pretty good about keeping up with the maintenance on it, or it wouldn’t have lasted so long, but the mileage it gets is abysmal and it fights for its life every ride because of how fast Phainon drives the little thing.

“It’s too small to be a boat,” Mydei tells him, and Phainon pretends to be upset but he laughs, and the wind blows the hair off his forehead, and he just looks… Charming. That’s probably a good word for him. It’s probably impossible to look at Phainon and dislike him.

“You suck and I hate you,” Phainon laughs, bringing them up the second incline, foot on the gas. As he catches up to a car ahead, he relaxes a little, no longer at the front of the line. “Walk home.”

“This is my car,” Mydei points out. “You can walk home.”

Phainon pretends to think about it. “But I’m taking the snacks,” he says.

“Damn,” Mydei retorts, “and I was so excited to eat those radioactive cheese crackers.”

A laugh. Phainon has a laugh like gold. “That’s right!” he exclaims. “Bow and grovel, and perhaps this venerable one shall take pity on you.”

“‘O Great Phainon of Myrtle Point, Oregon,” Mydei starts, tacking on Phainon’s hometown just to add words to the bullshit title.

“Yes, Devoted One,” Phainon says, deepening his voice like he’s the main character of a fantasy movie or narrating a car commercial. “Your God listens.”

Mydei flips up both middle fingers and says, “Go fuck yourself.”

They devolve into laughter from there. Phainon gets them up the incline, past the edge of the mountain, and the sun comes out, about to set, casting everything in gold. The road, the steep, forested drop to their right, blocked with a guard rail. Below that, city and nature sprawl out. Warm wind hits Mydei’s face as he turns his body to look out the window, tasting the air, kind of awed by the beauty of it.

“I’m stopping at the overlook,” Phainon informs him, and he doesn’t see any reason to protest. The car pulls into the tiny gravel parking lot marking the place, and they roll up their windows and slip out of the car to look, feet crunching in the rocks, the backs of their shirts soaked in sweat from sitting so long.

There’s a stone half wall blocking the edge, built from red and gray bricks and reaching about waist height. The top is coated with a smattering of bird poop, and there are a couple of placards that Mydei doesn’t bother to read as he steps up to look at the view, Phainon at his shoulder.

They’re lucky, because they’re the only ones here. It’s a small overlook, not half as big and touristy as some that he’s seen, but it isn’t lacking for that, not at all.

The hiss of wind through leaves, pulling hair out of Mydei’s ponytail. The air is sweet and fresh. Still warm, but not baking in the way it would be earlier in the day. He squints as he looks out. Directly below them, a pale stone cliff face, rough and textured from weather, scraggly trees rooted in place. Further out, rich green forest and the city, so huge and so tiny at once. They can see suburbs and tall city buildings. A sky that stretches endlessly, pale blue and spotted with clouds, a blinding sun over the horizon. Now, he shields his eyes and takes his phone out for a picture. He takes two in landscape mode so he can choose which one came out better later, and then he slips it back into his pocket.

“This view,” Phainon says, bracing his hands on a poopless spot of the half wall. “Goddamn.” It’s beautiful. A bit painful to look at, what with where the sun is. Phainon is squinting a bit, hair flipped off his forehead by the breeze, the light casting him in warm gold. “Too bad we aren’t here like twenty minutes later. The sunsets have to be amazing from here.”

“I’m sure,” Mydei agrees. The sun on Phainon’s neck, banded by his choker. His shirt collar flaps against him in the breeze. Mydei’s gaze is stuck on the bowl of his throat. “It’s beautiful.”

A soft hum. Phainon rocks on his heels, but he doesn’t turn to Mydei as he replies, “Look at the view when you say that, not at me.”

Gold in his hair, on his neck. Mydei sighs, turns back to the view. Their shoulders brush when he bends forward to lean on the wall, forearms folded atop it, back rounded. Hot, coarse stone. The soft fabric of Phainon’s t-shirt against his bare arm. “What an ego,” he murmurs, “to assume I was talking about you.”

Phainon mirrors his position, and nevermind that they have a dozen yards of the wall to themselves, he picks the spot right next to Mydei, close enough that their arms press tight together. Mydei is probably tacky with sweat. Their triceps will stick when they pull apart.

“What, you weren’t?” Phainon gives this soft laugh, more air than sound. “You’ve been looking at me all day, don’t think I don’t notice that, even when I’m driving.”

Mydei’s been dancing like a goddamn monkey for him for how long now? He doesn’t even know. So long he’s lost track of it. But no one counts their breaths, no one measures each and every beat of their heart. Of course he wouldn’t be able to pinpoint when it started beating for Phainon. What does it matter, to let it beat like that a little longer.

“What was it that you said the other day, ‘I’m always looking at you?’”

Phainon rocks into him a little. “And you know what you said after?”

“‘That’s a weird fucking thing to say.’”

Again, Phainon does that same laugh. The soft one, like a setting sun. “How the tables have turned,” he says. He sounds lighter, less bogged down by his grief, happier since he saw Cyrene. Mydei hopes it stays that way. Loves him happy but hates to make him happy, to be the cause of it, because it makes him feel like his stomach could turn inside out and like this could be permanent and real, and not just something Phainon plays around with on a whim. “So you were talking about me.”

A breath. Something flips inside him, climbs up his throat, whispers that this could be it. Maybe he wants you too, maybe he’s just as sick of pretending as you are. “Do you really want me to answer that question?”

Are you ready? Mydei wonders. Can we finally have this conversation now?

Phainon turns to look at him. He’s close, but Mydei already knew that. His eyes are bluer than the sky or the sea. “Maybe…” He wets his lips, flicks his gaze between each of Mydei’s eyes. “Maybe I do.”

Mydei studies him back. His hair in the breeze. His parted mouth, his open, kind of hopeful expression. Strangely, the panicked, fluttery thing sitting in Mydei’s chest calms. Like listening to his own heartbeat, like counting his breaths. He lets the silence stretch a little longer, just to see if Phainon will turn away and laugh it off like some kind of joke. But he just stays, just looks. They’re both always looking at each other.

“Yes, then,” Mydei says. He’s always been disgustingly sappy on the inside. A hopeless romantic, as much as he tries to hide it. Phainon tends to run into things head first, but even he’s cautious when it comes to this. “I think you’re beautiful.”

He can hear Phainon’s inhale, his hitch of breath. A second goes by, and then Phainon is turning away and covering his mouth. The shell of his ear goes crimson as Mydei watches, this feeling blooming in his chest. Warmth crawls up his neck. He’s sure he’s blushing too. He turns back to the view to map the lines of streets with his eyes, clearing his throat.

“Phainon,” he gets out, helpless.

“Sorry,” Phainon replies. His voice sounds all weird. He clears his throat too. “Sorry, I wasn’t expecting you to just say it.”

“You asked for it,” Mydei reminds him.

“Yeah,” Phainon breathes. His laugh is kind of overwhelmed. “It’s, um. It’s mutual, by the way. I think you’re beautiful too.”

Mydei can feel how red he must be. He ducks to hide his face in his arms. “Shut up if you’re going to be weird,” he grumbles. Another chuckle. Phainon bumps him again, draws away, their tacky skin sticking.

“Mydei,” he tries.

“Whenever you’re ready,” Mydei says into his arms. He can feel Phainon duck closer to him to hear, can see the fall of his shadow in his periphery.

“What?”

“Whenever you’re ready,” Mydei says. “I’ll say it back. So don’t bother if you don’t mean it.”

“Oh,” Phainon says. A pause. He’s always been so smart but so fucking stupid. “Oh. Mydeimos.” Mydei doesn’t raise his head. Just stares at the bird shit stains on the wall and tries not to burn into a crisp. It doesn’t help that Phainon is like the goddamn sun. Too close. Too bright. His stupid fucking smile is imprinted on the backs of Mydei’s eyelids, and it isn’t fair at all. “Mydei,” Phainon says again.

“Fucking what?” Mydei asks, turning just enough to look at him out of one eye through a curtain of hair.

“I’m in love with you,” Phainon says, as easy as breathing. Because what is there to be afraid of? That’s just his heart, bloody and beating in his chest, in his throat, in his open palms between them on the wall, dripping red on the bird shit, forming puddles, staining their clothes, slicking their hands.

“You can’t fucking laugh about it this time.”

“Mydei,” Phainon says, like he likes the taste of it in his mouth. “When was I ever the one who laughed?”

And he’s right. He might not say it like he means it, but he never laughs. Mydei does. And Mydei’s the one who never says it back. He sighs, and he can’t look at Phainon as he says it. “Me too.”

Another bump. Phainon reaches out and lightly guides Mydei’s chin up with the backs of his fingers. It’s a tiny, fleeting touch, and he pulls away as soon as Mydei is looking at him. He seems so hopeful, expression open, holding his breath like he needs to hear Mydei say it. “That doesn’t count,” he whispers, baiting him, and Mydei might as well be the fish on his Master Baiter t-shirt, because he’s always caught, always pulled along by some string connecting him to Phainon by a hook in the heart.

Another day, Mydei would probably laugh him off and call him needy, but he gets it. He needed to hear it too, and Phainon gave it to him so readily. God. He sucks in a breath.

“Why are you bracing yourself for it?” Phainon laughs. “You look like you’re taking a shit; you’ll hurt my feelings.”

“You’re a fucking idiot,” Mydei says, looking at his stupid smile. His heart flips, flips, flips. His ears are molten, and he’s just… “I’m in love with you.”

Phainon is quiet. His mouth spasms and he turns away again, having the exact same reaction to this as he did to Mydei calling him beautiful. He clears his throat, covers his mouth, hides his face in his arms. “Fuck,” he says, inhaling it, sounding breathless. “I’m gonna throw up.”

“The fuck do you mean you’re gonna throw up?” Mydei shoves him in the shoulder, and he laughs, laughs, laughs, stumbling a step away, still hiding in his arms. “Whose feelings are hurt now, asshole?”

“Sorry!” Phainon says, surfacing. He’s red from the neck up, smiling hard enough to squeeze tears out of his eyes. “I just… my butterflies have butterflies, man, I—”

“Shut up,” Mydei says, grabbing his collar to shake him a little, gritting his teeth, hating how much he loves this stupid fucking smile, this stupid fucking man. But he can’t even be mad, because he’s never met anyone quite so good as Phainon. Warm and earnest… and Mydei’s match, his equal, like they’re fucking Ancient Kremnoans. They’d battle for ten goddamn days and ten goddamn nights and there would never be a clear victor, and it’s so stupid and unfair how much Mydei likes that.

“Shut up,” Mydei says again, quieter, looking at him, loving him, and just… They’ve been here long enough for the sunset to start, just barely, just the first bits of orange and red painting the horizon, still shining down on them just a bit too much, and it’s so unfair that Mydei has to feel this way. But how could he not? Looking at Phainon now, how could he not?

His hand still balled up in Phainon’s shirt. He’ll stretch it out and leave wrinkles. Phainon is done laughing, just looking at him, wide-eyed and soft-mouthed and gold in the sun, flourishing and photosynthesizing in it like some kind of plant, and it isn’t fair at all. His knuckles against Phainon’s chest. His hand smooths out, slides up Phainon’s shoulder, around the back of his neck. It would be so easy to just… kiss him, or something. Really, what’s stopping him? He’s been waiting so goddamn long already.

Funny, Phainon kisses him first. He just sucks in this little breath and comes closer. He probably sees the look in Mydei’s eyes telling him to stop being such a fucking coward, because he leans in, hesitates for just a second, and then he fits their mouths together sweet and easy like he’s done it a hundred times. It’s a little dry and a little wet at once, close-mouthed and just the right amount of pressure.

He smells faintly like sunscreen, like coconut and summer, and he sets one hand on Mydei’s shoulder, the other barely brushing fingertips along the underside of his jaw. He’s less eager than Mydei anticipated. He always imagined Phainon coming in with too much force, clacking their teeth together, drawing away with a sheepish apology. He’d imagined a bit too much tongue and energy, because that’s how Phainon does everything. Whole-hearted and clumsy, with dog-like enthusiasm.

Maybe if it were his first, that would make sense, but Phainon has had a couple of boyfriends and girlfriends in the past, so of course he knows how to do this. It’s probably better this way. Mydei doesn’t think he’d be a very good teacher, if Phainon needed to learn.

“Is that fine?” Phainon asks, drawing away so he can breathe, still close enough that Mydei has to go cross-eyed to look at him. He sounds hopeful and uncertain in equal measure, like Mydei wouldn’t have just shoved him off and sworn at him if that wasn’t okay. He’s so dumb sometimes. So fucking sweet.

“You always pick the weirdest things to worry about,” Mydei informs him, and kisses him again, a little firmer this time, because gentle doesn’t come quite as easily to Mydei as it seems to for Phainon. His nose digs into Phainon’s cheek. There’s a sound as he pulls back. “I’d kick your ass if it wasn’t fine.”

“Should’ve figured,” Phainon says. One more kiss. Halfway through, he starts to smile, and Mydei gets his teeth.

“Quit that,” he murmurs, both arms finding their way around Phainon’s shoulders. Phainon’s lips are weird and firm as he tries to fight his smile, and Mydei gets his teeth again after half a second. “Fucking gross,” he says, giving up, just standing their foreheads pressed together.

“Sorry,” Phainon breathes. His hands find Mydei’s waist, finally touching like he’s allowed. “I’m just… happy, I guess. More than I have been in a while.”

A nicer version of Mydei might say something sweet. You deserve to be, or, you make me happy too. This one doesn’t, though. This one just says, “About fucking time,” and Phainon laughs, laughs, laughs with the sun in his hair and in his squinting eyes. They’ve wasted way too much time at this overlook, wind in their faces, the sound of an occasional car speeding past behind them. They’re going to be so late to the hotel, but Mydei can’t even bring himself to care.

chapters.title: Chapter 8
chapters.html:
Phainon falls asleep with relative ease that night, more than exhausted from the drive and the sun in his eyes. They reach the hotel a bit after midnight, change into pajamas and brush their teeth, and are in bed before one. Phainon thinks blurry thoughts and listens to Mydei’s breath beside him, and falls asleep within twenty minutes.

When he wakes, it’s to sweat-soaked sheets and clothing, Mydei’s face in his shoulder, and his left leg completely devoid of feeling where Mydei has it clamped between his. There’s a hand over his waist, and they’re touching in half a dozen spots, but nothing about this is comfortable enough to be considered cuddling. There’s a spot of drool on his sleeve.

Slowly and carefully, he attempts to extricate himself, if only to save his leg and get a head start on showering before Mydei can wake and claim it first. His leg seizes in bloodless pain, and Mydei’s hand unconsciously tightens. Phainon winces, pauses, and tries again, pulling his leg free and untangling Mydei’s fingers from his shirt. He’s reluctant to let go, so Phainon gives him a pillow to hold instead and sits up. The sensation of blood flowing back into his leg just about paralyzes him, and as he sits there and waits for the pins and needles to start, he watches Mydei press his face into the pillow and mumble something in his sleep.

He’s shirtless, as he always is at night. Maybe this should do something to Phainon, especially after they kissed last night, after they finally addressed whatever it is that hangs between them, but it’s just Mydei. He’s shirtless at least forty percent of the time, and Phainon is used to it. He’s just Mydei, and nothing had been weird after they got back into the car and drove for another four hours, and somehow that’s his favorite part.

He doesn’t want things to change too much. He doesn’t want to lose Mydei as a friend to have him as more than that. He didn’t realize until just now that he’d been afraid of losing that ease, that familiarity, but that doesn’t even make sense, does it? They’re still them, Mydei’s still Mydei, and that’s… good.

The pins and needles hit. Phainon gingerly rotates his ankle and bends his knee, trying to end it faster, but it’s all he can do to sit here and bear it. Mydei sleeps on, drooling and oblivious, and it’s stupid how fond Phainon feels. Suffering must be a side effect of love. He bends to get his phone off the nightstand and takes the most unflattering photo of Mydei he can manage.

He opens his texts with Cyrene, attaching the image. Can you believe I kissed this guy last night?

It’s 7:43, but only a moment passes before she reads it. She’s like him, a difficult sleeper and an early riser. The medication is probably making it worse, with how often she’s forced to nap. He watches the dots as she types.

I’m just surprised it hasn’t happened before last night.

He sends a handful of question marks back, feeling his lips quirk as he watches her type again.

That’s your business, she sends first. Another message follows up the first. It’s not like I was going to meddle where I didn’t belong, but I could tell, obviously. A third message. I’m happy for you.

He wasn’t expecting her to be surprised. He’s fairly certain anyone who’s known him longer than a day could figure this much out. He and Mydei had both known too, they just… didn’t do anything about it. Most lackluster response, he sends.

Sorry, did you want more enthusiasm? She sends a mile long string of emojis back, from shocked faces to hearts to confetti, and he laughs through his nose before he shuts his phone off and sets it back on the nightstand.

His pins and needles are mostly gone, so he slips off the bed and digs for fresh clothes in his luggage so he can shower. They smell like Cyrene’s detergent, and he’s… happy. That’s probably the easiest word for it. He’s hopeful that things are starting to go well for him. That Cyrene will be okay, that Mydei will be happy with him too. God, it’s been a while since he woke up content like this.

His chest fills up with something bigger than him. Warmth, nostalgia, something just softer than guilt. He’s good at spoiling these things for himself, but he knows he needs to feel this much too. It’s too much to unpack all at once.

For now, he’ll let Mydei sleep a little longer, and then they can have breakfast and resume the journey back home.

△

Mydei is still half asleep at breakfast. He answers questions with hums and grunts, leans over his plate with both elbows on the table, and keeps his eyes closed for too long increments before he drags them back open and peels another wedge from the tangerine in ruins on his plate. Phainon lets him be, smiling to himself as he separates the crispy and soggy sides of his bacon.

“Wasteful,” Mydei murmurs, watching him abandon the soggy sides to die with a scrunched up napkin. Phainon just holds the strip he’d been working on out to him, waving it in the air so he can see just how limp and flaccid it is.

“Do you want it, then?”

Mydei’s glare doubles in strength when he’s sleepy like this. His eyes look so dead inside. “Get that out of my face,” he grumbles, jabbing his fork into some similarly soggy sausage. “Nine hours driving today, and you’re going first.”

“Fine by me,” Phainon chuckles. “Do you need a nap? I know you didn’t get a lot of sleep.”

“You didn’t either,” Mydei points out, rubbing the edge of one eye with the second knuckle on his thumb. “It’s fine. I’ll wake up eventually.”

And he does, albeit slowly. They pack up after breakfast, and as he combs out his slightly damp hair, he seems more than half alive, though he’s definitely still tired. Phainon wraps up his phone charge and does a scan of the room to make sure he hasn’t forgotten anything. He steals Mydei’s keys, since he’ll be driving anyway, tucking them into his pocket and dipping into the bathroom to watch Mydei finish up. He’s handling his bangs now, twisting them and clipping them to the top of his head before he pulls out his eyeliner pen. His gaze shifts to Phainon in the mirror as he takes off the cap.

“Did you forget something in here?” he asks, leaning over the counter to get closer to the mirror, pulling the skin around his eye taut. Phainon’s gaze flicks from him to the counter, back to his exposed forehead.

“...No,” he says. In one fluid motion, Mydei lines his eye in red, moving his hands away to look. He should look silly with his hair clipped like that. He kind of does, but it’s also kind of hot how smoothly he did that. His gaze lands on Phainon, heavy amber and molten.

“What is it, then?” he asks, leaning forward again to do the other side. Phainon’s fingers twitch on the doorframe.

“Well, I was going to ask if you were ready, but then I got distracted.”

A deep hum. “By?” The way Mydei does his other eye is just as smooth and practiced as the first.

“Uh… huh?”

Mydei checks to make sure his eyeliner is even. When he’s satisfied, he unclips his hair and shakes out his bangs, turning to face Phainon, and that’s not what he looks like, asleep and drooling, is it? “You were distracted by?” he reiterates.

“Take a guess,” Phainon says, and part of him wonders if he could just… He doesn’t know. Reach out, maybe. Mydei would probably let him, but he isn’t quite used to what that looks like yet, what that feels like. He knows Mydei about as well as he could hope to know anyone, and he’s felt this way about him forever, but he’s never really thought about it seriously. Should he now? Now that they’ve acted on whatever this is, now that they’ve acknowledged it and let it become real?

Mydei lifts an eyebrow. His eyeliner is just about perfect. Under the fluorescent bathroom light, he’s the realest kind of beautiful Phainon knows. “I think it’s pretty obvious.”

“Then why’d you ask?” Phainon watches as Mydei gathers up the last of his toiletries in a plastic gallon size bag he’s probably been reusing for a few years at this point. He doesn’t replace things unless they’re beyond repair. His pink duffle bag, his favorite ratty bath towel, his water bottle with a dozen dents and scratches in the paint and faded, peeling stickers. Phainon could probably fit on that list too, now that he thinks about it.

Mydei’s never  left him in all this time. Not in any way that matters.

“To see if you’d try to defend yourself,” Mydei answers, closing the bag and taking a step closer to turn off the light. Phainon blinks, and the bathroom goes dark, Mydei’s face half lit by the spill of light from the window on the far wall of the hotel room. He’s close, Phainon is used to him being close. He’s the same, but it’s different now. Maybe some things do change.

“Do I need to defend myself?” Phainon asks. He’s always found Mydei captivating. This much is nothing new, not even to Mydei.

“Are you going to move out of the doorway?”

“I could,” Phainon says, looking at him. He remembers the rush of it last night. Mydei calling him beautiful, Mydei saying he loves him, Mydei kissing him. His own stupid reactions. The way he could do nothing but blush and hide in his arms and say weird things. Embarrassment swells with the heat that climbs his neck. He steps out of the doorway.

Mydei slips past him and unzips his duffle bag to shove his toiletries inside. When he’s done, he does the same scan of the hotel room Phainon had, checking for anything he might’ve left behind. There’s nothing at all, because neither of them unpack, really. No more than plugging in their chargers and leaving their toothbrushes by the sink to dry. He turns around to find Phainon still red in the face, covering his mouth.

“What are you blushing for?”

“Nothing,” Phainon says. “I’m just vividly reliving every stupid thing I did last night.”

Mydei chuckles at this. “You didn’t do anything out of character, at least.”

“That’s worse, you realize,” Phainon points out. “That means I’m stupid all the time.”

“And you’re just now realizing?”

Admittedly, this startles a laugh out of him, and he moves his hand up to rub at his brow, shaking his head. “So merciless, Mydeimos,” he says. “Take pity, would you? I’m trying my best.”

“I’m sure you are,” Mydei says, fairly gently, by Mydei standards. He lifts his duffle bag off the bed and comes closer, dropping it at their sides. He pulls Phainon’s hand away from his face and lightly cups his jaw, leaning forward to press a kiss to his cheek, surprisingly soft and a little bit chapped. “Reminder that I didn’t kick your ass last night when you kissed me,” he says, stepping back and retrieving his bag. “Let’s go.”

△

Phainon manages to drive for two hours this time. Sometimes he can do more, and Mydei always can, but today his head is running with the winds and his leg is bouncing, fingers tapping, shoulders tensed and cheek gnawed to a mess of sores. He’s a live wire, maybe a danger to the road, and they’re running on a quarter tank of gas so he takes the next exit to fill up as an excuse. 

He uses the restroom at the gas station, though he doesn’t need to. Mydei waits for him when he comes back out, leaning against the side of his car, scrolling through something on his phone all easy, and as Phainon’s feet kick up rocks on the way back, he gets this odd feeling. A heartbeat he can feel in his chest, a little voice in the back of his mind saying this is weird.

He tosses the keys over, watches Mydei tuck his phone in his pocket and climb into the driver’s side. The car is hot and stinking of the lemon air freshener hanging from the mirror. He turns something on as they drive, girl groups, pop rock, guitar. He turns the music off. 

“Do you want to call your sister?” Mydei asks.

He should probably say yes. He should probably want to say yes. “Not right now,” he says instead. Mydei’s hum isn’t questioning, which he feels is a victory. He couldn’t answer if asked what’s wrong.

They’re so far from home, is this thought he keeps having. His mind will go to a dozen places just to end up back at this. So far from home. They’ll need another night in another hotel, another day on the road. It’s barely a blink. He isn’t bored, he isn’t lonely. He watches out the window; they’ve been in the middle of nowhere for a while. Acres and acres of farmland, nothing but fields or cattle grazing on either side. Miles and miles of gold rippling in the wind. He remembers the sound of that, the heat of the sun on his skin, the smell of the earth.

He hasn’t seen wheat in harvest season in a decade or longer. There’s a tight feeling in his throat. He sucks in a shaky breath.

Still here, he thinks, blinking to the afterimage of clouds and swaying wheat. It never really goes away, does it? That feeling. Homesickness for somewhere that doesn’t exist. Missing people and things that are long gone. He still thinks about them all the time. He doesn’t think he’ll ever stop. He wonders if Cyrene feels that too. Realizes that one day, one of them will be stuck missing the other. He thinks about that all the time too.

He clears his throat, unlocks his phone to dredge up a song. “I thought of something you can learn on guitar,” he tells Mydei, who’s been quiet enough that he probably knows whatever’s going on in Phainon’s head. He’ll never say it, but he picks up on the strangest things. He burns incense instead of candles because he knows Phainon is afraid of the flame. He stays silent as they drive through some boring old wheat fields because he knows Phainon is feeling nostalgic.

The rumble of the road in his ears. The sun cooking his right arm and reflecting off his phone screen as he finds what he’s looking for. The silence is replaced by the opening chords of the song. Mydei doesn’t seem to recognize it at first, but he barks a laugh as the singer comes in. “Today is gonna be the day—”

He skips it with a button on the dash. “Fuck off,” he says, and Phainon has to laugh too. “I’m not learning Wonderwall.”

△

They get Greek food for lunch, and Mydei’s gyro is so good he notes down the ingredients and vows to try to recreate it at home. Phainon holds his hand for about ten seconds before he psychs himself out of it, and then they’re back on the drive. He falls out of his funk after a while, and then he’s back to talking nonstop, though it seems he’s run out of conversation topics because he turns to asking strange questions that kind of piss Mydei off, like whether potatoes count as vegetables and if he’d rather fight a bear or fifty Canada geese.

Eventually, they call Cyrene. She describes her last day of treatment, says that her friends Dan Heng and Stelle both visited for the tail end of it. They’re going to take the IV out soon, and she can’t wait to not be tethered for it, even if it’s only for a short time between rounds of medication. They end up talking to her for an hour and twenty-three minutes before one of the doctors comes in to check on her and she has to hang up. Phainon does that thing again, where he’s happy and then he’s sad after all the talking is over. Mydei tells him another old Kremnoan story, this time of the rivalry of Nikador and Kephale, the Titans of Strife and Worldbearing in their mythology, and he perks right up.

Dinner is unfortunately greasy Chinese food. Phainon seems to enjoy it, but it makes Mydei feel slightly ill. He can’t wait to have his own kitchen again, and says so as they cut through the parking lot.

“You’ve had, what, a day without one?” Phainon asks. “You baked yesterday morning.”

“It’s been five meals,” Mydei notes, for reference. “Not only do I feel sick, my wallet feels sick as well.”

Phainon opens his mouth to refute this, but can’t. Breakfast was free at their hotel, but lunch and dinner are still on them, and it adds up. He takes the keys when Mydei passes them to him, locks the car and slips in. Mydei takes the passenger seat, since he’d driven for the last uneventful three hour stretch. As Phainon sets up his directions, he clears his throat.

“I could pay for you next time,” he says, like he’s trying to sound casual and failing grossly. “I mean, it’s only right if, um…”

“We are equally broke, Phainon,” Mydei reminds him. The car rumbles as it starts.

“So you can pay the time after that,” Phainon tries.

“And then we both still paid for two meals, and are just as broke.”

“You’re the worst,” Phainon says, and the bumper scrapes the curb as he pulls onto the street, nearly turning right when his directions tell him to turn left. He corrects it without incident and tries to play it off like that wouldn’t have ended in disaster if there were perhaps two more cars on the road. Mydei shakes his head and laughs a little, propping his elbow on the window to look outside, the sun hot on his exposed arm. The town they’re in is a small one, with old buildings and peeling paint, but it’s unmistakably cozy, so he doesn’t have a word of complaint.

“I’m just saying…” There’s an odd break in Phainon’s words as he clears his throat, checking each of his mirrors, visibly swallowing. “Maybe it won’t help us be less broke, but… Is this official? Like, well. Uh. Us? As a unit, or… That sounds weird. A couple? Or a, um, partnership?”

“What are we, corporations working together to exploit the poor?” Mydei asks, and watches Phainon go through the five stages of grief all in one go. His lips purse, part with a wet sound, red climbing up his neck as he lifts one hand off the steering wheel like he means to hide his face before he remembers that he’s driving and needs to be able to see.

“Admittedly, that came out wrong,” he says, settling on acceptance, tapping his fingers on the steering wheel, all four at once, minus his thumb, before he grips it like normal again, knuckles going white. “I meant something less like exploiting the poor and more like…” He thinks for a moment, Mydei trying his best to keep his expression neutral, despite the way his mouth wavers and tries to edge into a smile.

“Like what?” he prompts. “A peace treaty to defeat a common enemy?”

Phainon laughs through his nose. “You know you suck, right?”

“Perhaps a contract to split the spoils of war?”

“Like…” Phainon opens his mouth, closes it, scratches his head as he thinks about it. “Like…” He squints at the directions, gets over one lane so he can turn left at the next light. His tongue flicks out to wet his lips. “Yeah, fuck, I’ve got nothing.”

“There’s gotta be a record for how goddamn awkward you are,” Mydei tells him. “Maybe you could make it into the next Guiness book.”

Phainon glances at him, sunglasses on, reflecting Mydei back at himself. “You’re not even going to try to help me? You’re just going to sit there and watch me suffer?”

“Yeah,” Mydei says, plucking his phone out of his lap to add another song to the queue. A solid four minutes and fifty-five seconds of alternative rock to match the last six songs he’s played of the same genre. Phainon flip flops between vibes on a whim, adding soft pop next to loud electronic dance music, next to showtunes. Mydei likes to stay consistent and transition slowly. “I’m having a pretty good time.”

“What a kind, gentle, doting lover you are,” Phainon tells him. “You really make me feel so warm and fuzzy and cared about inside.”

“Glad to see my efforts acknowledged,” Mydei says sarcastically. The last song fades out, and the next comes on. “I really try.”

“Uh huh,” Phainon says, bobbing his head up and down. “And you succeed.”

“I know I do.”

An exhale, somewhere between a laugh and a sigh. Phainon shifts in his seat, grips the steering wheel a bit tighter, leg bouncing to the beat. “So I guess I have to say it properly, right? Will you be my boyfriend?”

“Is that supposed to be sarcastic too?” Mydei asks, but Phainon doesn’t seem to find this funny. Maybe they’re too used to pretending this is some kind of joke. They’ll have to work on that, learning how to treat this seriously.

“Fuck off,” Phainon says. “No. I mean it, but I can take it back if you’re going to be an asshole.”

“Sorry,” Mydei says. “Habits die hard.”

“Answer the question.”

“Yes.” This comes out surprisingly simply. He doesn’t know why he’d expected it to be hard. Things are rarely straightforward between them, but this comes out easily once Phainon figured out how to ask. “I’d like that.”

“Cool,” Phainon says, nodding, lifting one hand off the steering wheel to wipe it on his pants, then the other. His expression is carefully blank, but his ear—only half hidden by his hair—is bright red, and his mouth twitches before he purses his lips to stop himself from smiling like a buffoon. He clears his throat. “To a successful partnership, then.”

“We split the profits fifty-fifty,” Mydei tells him.

A weak laugh. “What exactly constitutes the profits?” he asks, and honest to god scratches his chin like a cartoon character while he thinks about it. “Actually, don’t answer that.”

Mydei squints at him. “Clearly you’re the one with an answer,” he points out. “What’s that face for? You’re not thinking something weird, are you?”

“No!” Phainon says, too quickly. “I have never had an untoward thought in my life.”

“Who said anything about untoward?”

Phainon goes quiet, whether at a loss for words or unwilling to dig himself a deeper hole. Mydei laughs, just a chuckle at first, and then with his full chest.

“Shut up,” Phainon protests, helpless. “Stop laughing, Mydeimos, I mean it.”

“Yeah, sure.” He laughs a little longer, sighs as he looks at the downturned corners of Phainon’s mouth. After a breath, he manages a straight face. “So what kind of thoughts were you having?”

Phainon doesn’t even look at him, just extends one arm, middle finger flipped up. Another laugh, Mydei bats his hand away. “How romantic.”

“You know it.” Now, Phainon smiles, pulling onto the freeway, shutting his phone off and shoving it in his pocket since he doesn’t really need directions to drive straight for three hundred miles. He pushes the sunglasses up his nose, smiles with teeth before he squashes it down to something more subtle. “You lucked out, you know. You’ve got a damn good boyfriend.”

“You were really just waiting for a chance to call yourself my boyfriend, weren’t you?”

“You know it,” Phainon repeats. Mydei shakes his head, chuckles.

“My mother is going to have a field day with this,” he mutters, thinking of the way she always asks about Phainon when she calls, the way she never outright tries to push Mydei towards him, but can see through him like glass. They’d just been talking, once, and Mydei was telling her about driving to a party an hour away just to rescue Phainon from a couple of drunk friends. She’d laughed over the phone, warm and crackly, and said, you give your all to that boy, don’t you? He thinks about that all the time, the same way he thinks about her grabbing Phainon by the face and later saying, he grew up beautiful, like Mydei isn’t haunted by that fact every day.

She raised him to love with everything he has. She’ll probably laugh when he tells her, call him a coward for taking so long, but she’ll be proud.

“Your mother?” Phainon asks.

“Yes,” Mydei sighs. “My mother.”

Phainon glances at him, turning the air conditioning up one setting higher. “How so?”

And he dug himself into that hole, didn’t he? Mydei sighs, traces patterns over his phonecase. “My mother loves you, in case you haven’t noticed. Remember that one year you went with me for Christmas and she grabbed your face and inspected you? She pulled me aside later just to tell me you grew up beautiful and that your neck tattoo means you must be strong and worthy.”

“Wha—” Phainon makes a strange, confused sound. “That whole time she was so scary,” he says, and laughs incredulously. “I thought she hated me!”

“Quit laughing,” Mydei says, “it’s not like it’s funny.”

“Oh, but it is,” Phainon protests. Another split second laugh, Mydei is hit with the force of his grin, stretching too wide for the complete lack of hilarity of the situation. “Tell me, did she say anything else?”

“I don’t think I want to tell you if she did,” Mydei tells him. “Not if you’re going to make it weird and embarrassing.”

A contemplative hum. Phainon hooks a finger under his choker as he considers this. “Very well,” he says, “this venerable one is kind and benevolent, and will offer you a piece of his own embarrassing information in exchange.”

“You say that like I don’t have enough dirt on you already,” Mydei says.

“Come on,” Phainon tries. “Please? You’d be totally curious if Cyrene said something about you, wouldn’t you? Help a guy out.”

“Bow and grovel,” Mydei says.

Phainon clears his throat, and something like dread settles in Mydei’s stomach. “Please,” Phainon says. “Please, Mydei? Please, I need to know, I’ll tell you something so embarrassing after, I promise it’ll be worth it, please. Please, Mydeimos, plea—”

“Shut up,” Mydei says, wanting to kick him if they weren’t in the car, a laugh betraying his words. “You’re so goddamn annoying.”

The edge of Phainon’s smile. He’s still looking at the road, tapping out the music that fills their silences. “...So?” he prompts.

Mydei sighs. “Last Christmas, I went up and we were looking at our old picture books and shit. She was telling me about my dad before he became a total deadbeat and died, and she looks at me and goes, love doesn’t wait for cowards, Mydeimos, it’s always better to feel and hurt now than to regret wasting the chance later. And then she closes the books and asks how you’re doing. She’ll never meddle, but I swear to god she’s never been so obvious.”

Phainon laughs a little, and then he chews on his cheek. “Christmas,” he says. “Just how long have you liked me, Mydeimos?”

“Christmas wasn’t even that long ago,” Mydei grumbles.

“It’s probably been years for me,” Phainon admits. “I can’t even pinpoint a time, it’s just kind of been there forever.” Why is it so easy to say these things for him? Mydei has to dig the words out like sticking a hand down his throat.

Heat crawls up his face. Mydei turns toward the window and brings a hand to tug at his ear. “Me too,” he gets out. In his peripheral, Phainon is doing that red faced, twitchy mouthed smile again. He looks away, watching the billboards and the buildings fly by. “It’s your turn to say something embarrassing, by the way.”

“Right,” Phainon laughs. “Let me think; I feel like you already know the worst of it.”

“You didn’t even have something in mind?” Mydei huffs. “What a fucking scam.”

“Shh,” Phainon hushes him. “Let me think.” He’s quiet for a bit, chewing on his cheek again, humming softly. He inhales. “You have to promise not to laugh, but I’ve got something.”

“Yeah, fuck that. You laughed at everything I said.” Phainon scoffs, goes quiet again. “Are you going to say it?”

“It’s…” He sighs out of his nose. “Fine. I have… somewhere, buried in the trenches of my notes app—”

“The more you lead up to it, the more embarrassing it gets,” Mydei tells him. “Just like a minute ago, when you asked me to be your boyfriend.”

“Shut up,” Phainon says, and pouts a little. “Fine, I’ll just…” He takes a deep breath, like he really is embarrassed about whatever it is that he’s going to say and needs to work himself up to it. “In my notes app, I have…” He scratches his nose, clears his throat. “A list of places I’d like to be kissed.”

There’s a pause, both of them silent. Mydei opens his mouth to speak. “And what’s on it?”

Phainon groans, looks like he would very much like to bury his face in his arms if he weren’t driving. “I’d really rather not answer that. Besides, I’ve already fulfilled my end of the deal; you don’t need to know any more.”

“Wouldn’t it be good for you to tell me?” Mydei points out. “Realistically, I’m the only one who can check anything on that list off anytime soon.”

“Don’t say that,” Phainon says, voice cracking, red down to his neck. “Don’t fucking say that, oh my god.”

“Mainly I’m just curious,” Mydei says, smoothing out his expression, because Phainon probably would die on the spot if he started laughing. “By ‘places’ do you mean locations, like… ‘at a scenic overlook next to a pile of bird shit,’ or body parts like ‘the back of my neck,’ or, ‘my knees,’ or some shit.”

“My knees?” Phainon asks. “That’s what you chose as an example?”

“Fuck off, is ‘my armpits’ better?”

“No!” He’s laughing now, which is what Mydei had been hoping for. Phainon feels shame too easily. And something like this… it’s embarrassing, sure, but Mydei daydreams weird shit too, even if he doesn’t go as far as to write it down. “That’s a hundred times worse!” 

Mydei lets his laughter die down. The flush doesn’t quite fade, but Phainon no longer looks like he’s going to crash the car and find somewhere to bury himself. Mydei gives him another breath, then says, “So… Body parts?”

“I hope you’re not imagining this freakishly large list with weird shit like knees and armpits,” Phainon says. “It’s like… six bullet points, and they’re all normal, and I made it like… three years ago.”

“Why are you so embarrassed about it, then?” Phainon glances at him, and oh, Mydei’s reflection in the sunglasses looks smug. He crosses his arms and sucks on his teeth.

“You try telling someone you’ve thought about them kissing your eyelids with a straight face,” Phainon says. “It’s weird! It’s embarrassing! I’ve been dating you for less than twenty-four hours!”

“So that’s one of them, then.”

“Shut up.” Phainon sniffs, checks his blind spot to pass a slow car. “Yes.”

Mydei is so ridiculously fond of him. It isn’t fair. There’s only so much room in his heart, full to bursting. “You’re making it a way bigger deal than it really is,” he says. “I’ll tease you a little, because it is kind of funny, but you can ask me for things, you know? The worst I can do is say no.”

“The worst you can do is make fun of me ruthlessly, and then say no,” Phainon corrects. “And I don’t know, but that seems like a pretty likely outcome.”

“Am I doing that now?”

At this, Phainon pauses, finally listens to what Mydei is saying. “Well,” he says, wetting his lips, “no.”
