They get to the hotel with the last dying rays of sun. Check in is easy at this hour, and then they’re dragging their luggage into the elevator, up to the third floor, and into their room. It’s dark and cool with working air conditioning, and they leave their stuff in the entryway. The door shuts too loudly as they close it again to head back out.

There’s a warm wind outside. The worst of the heat is past, and the sun is already hanging low in the sky as they walk, so it isn’t too bad. Mydei is glad for a chance to stretch his legs, his whole body kind of stiff and aching from spending the past two days in the car. Phainon just likes walking; he’ll go out on a whim and wander until Mydei has to call him and say, Where the fuck are you? Dinner’s ready.

They’re on the outskirts of the city this time, somewhere between suburbs and downtown, with aged, squat houses and not too busy streets. Phainon turns them left at the corner, so the sun is at their backs. Side by side, he walks too close. Their shoulders bump. His hand is shoved deep in his pocket or Mydei might’ve reached out to hold it.

“Sick of me yet?” Phainon asks, bumping him again, doing it on purpose because he’s like glue in a different way than Mydei is. Phainon likes proximity, always touching, always talking. Mydei is content to just be in the same room.

“When am I not?” Mydei says instead of answering with something stupid like no, never, or, I like spending time with you. There are a handful of orange cones blocking an exposed pipeline on the side of the street. Dug up dirt underfoot, spread to the sidewalk by the wind.

“Most of the time, probably,” Phainon answers, sliding his hands out of his pockets to stretch them overhead with an exaggerated sound. When he drops his arms, they bump again. “Otherwise you wouldn’t put up with me half as much.” Cracks in the sidewalk. Faded white paint for a crosswalk. There’s nobody coming, so they cross, drifting a little further apart, then back together as they wind up on the narrow sidewalk again.

“If you know that much, why bother asking,” Mydei mutters, not really making it a question. Ahead, there’s a bit of movement. He hears Phainon suck in a breath. A handful of steps forward, and he crouches. In the driveway of this next house, just under a dirt-covered, off-white pickup truck, sits a gray tabby cat. A little scruffy, but collared. It stares at them with wide eyes and an upturned, sniffing nose. Phainon looks at it and blinks slowly, trying to get it to trust him as he inches forward. When he’s close enough, maybe two yards away, he sits right there on the ground and holds out a hand.

“Hey buddy,” he murmurs, all soft and high pitched. He uses this voice with any small animal ever, though he speaks normally with kids. Mydei watches him, tired and fond, and yes, maybe a little bit sick of him. He sighs as comes to sit next to him on the sidewalk. The cat doesn’t even flinch, and when he holds a hand out, it comes to Mydei first.

“This isn’t fair at all,” Phainon says as Mydei sits through a thorough examination as the cat smells his outstretched fingers. After a bit, it nudges its head against them, so he pets it once, twice, all the way to its tail, scratching its low back a bit. The cat turns around, and he can see that she’s a girl as she walks a little lap around them, sniffing the back of Phainon’s shirt as he holds carefully still.

“She’s friendly,” Mydei tells him, taking his hand and holding it out for the cat to sniff. After she does, she bumps her head into Phainon’s hand the same she had to Mydei, and Phainon makes a distressed sound as he pets her.

“What a gal,” he says, scratching her head. “What a lady.”

She comes back to Mydei, putting her paws on his lap as he rubs his thumbs over the thinner patches of fur in front of her ears. She tips her face up, eyes squeezing shut as she leans into the touch. Phainon’s head falls onto his shoulder, hair tickling his cheek. “You’ll make me jealous,” he says.

“Of who?” Mydei asks. “Me, or the cat?”

A petulant sound. Phainon reaches up to cup his cheek, turning Mydei so they’re facing each other. His hands falter on the cat’s head. Phainon is kind of glaring at him, close enough to kiss.

“The cat, then,” Mydei says, answering his own question.

“Fuck off,” Phainon grumbles, and lets go of his face. He’s quiet for a bit, sliding his fingers through the cat’s fur when she comes back to him before she gets distracted by the grass and ignores them completely to gnaw on it. He sighs, softly, bends to touch her and gets ignored some more.

Mydei chuckles softly. “Come on,” he says. “We probably look weird, sitting in front of someone’s house like this. Let’s go.”

“But the best girl ever,” Phainon protests.

“She’s not your cat, Phainon, let’s go.”

“Our cat.”

Mydei stands up, scraping the sidewalk, brushing himself off. He holds out a hand. Phainon sighs and takes it, heaving himself up, casting forlorn glances back toward the cat as Mydei pulls him along. He’d taken Mydei’s right hand with his left, and neither of them has let go. Mydei under the guise of dragging him, Phainon under the guise of being dragged. Even now, they come up with flimsy excuses. Not looking, not drawing attention to it, Mydei adjusts the fit of their hands. Phainon opens his fingers, Mydei slots his between them, and they walk.

Stupid, stupid, stupid, how it probably makes him blush. He can feel the heat in his face. The sweat in his palms. Phainon doesn’t comment, and he’s glad.

They’re quiet for a while. The gold of the dying sun turns to the blue beginnings of dusk. Their hands sway at their sides. Their shoulders keep bumping.

“Do you think a lot of things are going to change between us?” Phainon asks, looking at the weeds growing in the sidewalk cracks instead of Mydei. Their hands are clammy. They should probably let go, but somehow that’s just as awkward as initiating it.

Mydei turns to him, his profile, the cut of his jaw and the two pimples stacked on his cheek. “What do you mean?”

“Just… things, I don’t know,” Phainon tries. “Are we going to turn into something different?”

Still, stubbornly, Phainon doesn’t look at him. His eyes are how to read him, clear blue, with lighter patterning in the irises. “I still don’t understand what you’re asking,” Mydei tells him. “It’s not like we’re going to become completely different people, but… yeah. Some things will change.” They already have, he doesn’t say. They wouldn’t be holding hands if nothing changed, Mydei wouldn’t have kissed his cheek this morning, wouldn’t have kissed him on the mouth last night. Without change, what’s the point of honesty?

“You’re right,” Phainon admits. He pulls his hand free, wipes it on his pants, laughs a little. “Sorry, I’m sweaty.”

“I noticed,” Mydei says, and wipes his hand too. “Me too, but I didn’t know how to let go.”

“What?” Phainon laughs, seeming to find this amusing. Mydei can only tolerate him for his smile. He’d do too many things for it.

“I don’t know, it felt… mean, I guess.”

His laugh is softer this time, though Mydei is well aware that his words have become even more ridiculous. “Nah,” Phainon says. “Just let go next time; my feelings won’t be hurt.” He wipes his hands once more, holds it out again. “And then when our hands are dry, we can hold hands again and it won’t be disgusting.”

Mydei stares at his hand. Hates the way his heart clamors in his chest. He takes Phainon’s hand again, though both of them are still a bit damp. “I guess so,” he says, and adds, because Phainon is still being weird, “this is a change, you know.”

They make another left, Phainon leading them in a big, square loop. Shadows start to settle. They’ll want to get back soon, before it’s truly dark. He’s beautiful still, but Mydei can’t help but think Phainon is better suited to the sun.

“I guess I hadn’t thought of it like that,” Phainon murmurs, looking at their hands, then back in front of him. The pools of light from the streetlamps, windows lit up from inside.

“Chronic worrier,” Mydei teases him. It comes out gentler than he means it to. Everything does these days, and it’s a goddamn illness. “Not everything ends in disaster.”

“Least of all you,” Phainon breathes. He squeezes Mydei’s hand, and… it’s nice to see him recognize that Mydei is steady, that after all these long years, he’s finally figured out that he doesn’t have plans to do anything but stay. Maybe it’s Mydei’s fault for never saying it aloud, but he doesn’t think he’s ever been subtle about Phainon.

“Least of all me,” he agrees, and watches the side of Phainon’s smile.

“You really love me, don’t you?”

“Shut up,” Mydei tells him. “Now you’re taking it too far.”

Chapter End Notes

tidbits (version 6.0): crazy take I know, but Phainon is the one with more relationship experience here... this Mydei turned out a lot more reserved compared to my versions of him in canonverse... and he's been too stuck on Phainon to really care about dating other people. Phainon says yes 9/10 times he's asked out because he likes getting to know people and is willing to try to let feelings grow... but it never works out longer than a month or two because he can never shake off his feelings for Mydei, and he doesn't really want to. so now they're here. awkward as fuck but in love or something

chapters.title: Chapter 9
chapters.html:
“It just hit me that I have to go back to work tomorrow,” Phainon says, his head pillowed on Mydei’s arm, staring at the play of light and shadows on the ceiling with the curtains pulled open. The hotel room is cold, but they’re sticky with body heat, already full from breakfast and procrastinating the drive home. Just one more day, but it’s another nine hours neither of them is looking forward to. “I don’t want to at all.”

Mydei laughs through his nose, bicep tensing as he bends his elbow to poke Phainon square in the forehead. “No one wants to go to work tomorrow,” he says, snorting at the way Phainon scrunches his face at him. His touch smoothes, gentles, fingers drifting to card through Phainon’s hair. “But we all need the money. So do you. That’s just life.”

He smells like this hotel’s soap of choice, they both do. Lemon verbena, weirdly strong. Phainon likes it and hates it in equal measure. “Oh, capitalist society,” he bemoans, turning his face into Mydei’s shirt, a small logo stitched on the chest. Mydei’s arm shifts around his shoulders; they fit with surprising ease. He supposes they have plenty of practice. This is one of those boundaries they’ve never hesitated to cross. “What if we went back to being hunter-gatherers?”

“Then we would die,” Mydei tells him, fingertips finding their way beneath his sleeve. With his other hand, he pokes Phainon in the forehead again. “Do you really think you’d be able to forage? Hunt something and kill it with your own hands?”

He doesn’t, but it hardly matters. Phainon lifts his head to look at him, locking their ankles together. “You’d take care of me, wouldn’t you?”

Mydei pokes him harder until he goes cross-eyed and frowns. “What makes you think I’d be able to do any of that?”

“You mean you can’t?” Phainon pretends to be shocked. Mydei scowls at him, but it isn’t like he means it. He has a scowl reserved just for Phainon, and he’ll never say it, but it’s fond. He’s always fond, Phainon is pretty sure. He can count the times he’s made Mydei seriously mad on one hand. They argue and get on each other’s nerves on the daily, but it never actually means anything. Not when they can have this too.

“HKS,” Mydei murmurs. Hyena, scoundrel, whatever that word means. He doesn’t say it all that often. His mother and father both spoke fluent Kremnoan, but he didn’t learn much growing up. Just words and phrases here and there. It’s a harsh language, but Phainon likes the sound of it on his tongue. In a way, he mourns for it too. Another dying culture, lost to the winds. Who would Mydei speak it to, even if he had learned it fluently? “We’re equally doomed in this scenario.”

Phainon pulls his hand off, pinning it beneath his own on Mydei’s chest. “Different scenario, then,” he tries, wedging the top half of his foot under Mydei’s calf, though it puts his knee hiked up and his hip twisted. “Hear me out. We homestead.”

“Phainon,” Mydei says.

“We’ll have goats,” Phainon says. “We’ll grow wheat and berries and potatoes. We’ll have a couple of cats as mousers. It’ll be great.”

“Goats,” Mydei repeats. Phainon smiles.

“Goats,” he agrees. “And chickens, and cows, maybe. Mousers for sure. An orange one and a white one. Meowdeimos and Furnon. They’ll compete over who can catch more mice, and they’ll always be hissing and fighting with each other, but then we’ll find them cuddling in the barn one day.”

“Sometimes I wonder if you hear the things that come out of your mouth,” Mydei tells him, fingers skimming up and down his arm. Phainon laughs a little, lifting his hand from Mydei’s to trace patterns on his ribs instead, shifting his hip, curling his leg around Mydei’s closer to him. “Meowdeimos and Furnon? Really?”

“They’ll be the best mousers,” Phainon confirms, tapping the foot not pinned beneath Mydei’s leg. His sock hisses against the sheets. Mydei kicks him lightly, trapped as he is.

“You move so goddamn much,” he says, pressing Phainon’s hand flat too, right over his left rib. His breath filters through Phainon’s hair, and when Phainon stills, he huffs. “Meowdeimos is the better of the two,” he says.

A laugh bubbles up in Phainon’s throat. “Oh, but you forget that Furnon has experience on a farm,” he says, and something bittersweet and nostalgic bubbles up with it. “He knows all the right places to look already. Meowdeimos is his fresh-faced little junior; of course he can’t compete.”

“Meowdeimos is a fast learner,” Mydei protests. “Give him a bit, and he’ll know all those things too.”

Phainon laughs softly. A breath, two, and he can’t stay still any longer, pulling his leg free to rock it from side to side. His knee keeps bumping Mydei, but he doesn’t get scolded for it. And god, what an odd blessing that it doesn’t bother him too much, that he plays along with all of Phainon’s dumb little daydreams. Cyrene is the same way, and Phainon is kind of lucky, isn’t he? To have two people who stay, two people who play along. “They’ll be equals, then,” he decides. “Some nights Furnon will catch more mice, and some nights Meowdeimos will, and we’ll never know who the better mouser is.”

Mydei’s chest shakes with his laughter. “And then we’ll find them cuddling in the barn,” he says, and throws his leg over Phainon’s to stop him from moving so much. Phainon just taps his fingers on Mydei’s ribs instead.

“See,” he says, smiling but keeping his eyes averted so Mydei can’t see how wet and shining they must be. He isn’t even sad. He’s happy, and somehow that’s harder. “You get it. We’ll be living the dream.”

“Sounds like a lot of work, just to get away from work,” Mydei points out.

“Ah, you’re right,” Phainon says, sweating with their combined body heat but unwilling to move. He could probably stay here for hours, if Mydei doesn’t get sick of all his moving first. “I’ll just win the lottery instead.”

Mydei barks a laugh. “Yeah, sure,” he says, and he holds Phainon so easily. Has it always been like that? He thinks it has. God knows how many nights he’s spent with his head in Mydei’s lap. “That’s way more realistic.”

“And then we’ll never have to work again,” Phainon says, laughing a little, rolling so he’s on his back and they’re side-by-side again, his head still pillowed on Mydei’s arm, their bodies still pressed tight. The sun has barely shifted when he looks at the way it paints the ceiling again. It’s still early, but soon it won’t be, and they can’t stay here forever. They have a home to get back to, after all. “I’ll share, you know. ‘Cause I’m nice like that. We can move somewhere nicer, and you won’t have to worry about a thing.”

Quiet. Just their breath, the sound of the air conditioning hissing through the vents. Crisp white sheets and pillows a bit too firm for Phainon’s liking. He’s been using the same flat, nasty yellow one at home for years now. He could probably hear Mydei’s heartbeat if he tried. His own if he held his breath. He wishes they had a balcony. He wants to go on the roof and feel the sun and the wind and smell the ocean, smell the earth. He’s always wanted way too many things.

“Phainon,” Mydei says, and his throat is tight. He could’ve cried seeing those wheat fields yesterday. What’s wrong with him? Why is it that the moment the smallest thing happens, he tips over the edge? Is it work stress or pressure or anxiety? Is it Cyrene’s illness and his premature grief? Is it still just homesickness, after all this time?

“Have I always been this much of a useless sap?” he asks. “I can’t remember, now that I’m thinking about it.”

“You’re too used to faking your smiles,” Mydei tells him.

“Maybe,” he admits. His chest hurts. “I miss home, Mydei. I miss my parents and I miss the ocean and the wheat fields and the neighbor kids. I miss Cyrene, and we just talked to her yesterday. It’s like that’s all there is. Just… so much missing.”

A hum. “And you’ll feel that forever,” Mydei says, not too softly. His arms flexes again as he reaches to play with Phainon’s hair. “That’s just life.”

Phainon takes a breath deep enough to make his chest hurt. Exhales it all at once. “I can’t even be mad about it,” he says. “The memories are too important to me, you know?”

The next pause can’t span more than a couple of breaths, but it feels like forever before Mydei speaks again. “I miss my dad,” he admits. “Have I ever told you that?”

“No,” Phainon whispers. “But I’ve always wondered. It can’t— I know he was a bad guy but… you don’t just walk away from your dad dying without a care in the world, no matter who he was.”

“I couldn’t even cry at his goddamn funeral,” Mydei says. “But I still wonder if he’d be proud of me when I do shit he’d have called strong. I still look at him in the pictures all over my mom’s house and wonder if maybe he wasn’t as bad as I remember him being.” He makes a frustrated sound. “I just… I feel those things too, even if it hardly compares to you losing everything in that fire. It doesn’t make you a useless sap. My… my mom would’ve said you’re stronger for it, to be able to carry all of those memories into the next day and the one after that, and my mom is never wrong about anything.”

Phainon laughs a little, throat tight, pursing his lips. He reaches over Mydei’s body for his free hand to squeeze, a bit awkward with their position, but… “Thanks,” he tries. “I think you found the magic words I needed to hear.”

“No I fucking did not,” Mydei says. “You still feel all of it, and you’re not going to stop, so shut up.”

He laughs harder, and then he’s probably crying, tears slipping from his eyes as he drags himself to sit upright, wiping his cheeks with the backs of his hands, sniffling. “Ah, fuck,” he says as Mydei sits up too. “Quit looking at me.”

“Shut up,” Mydei tells him, and there are too warm arms wrapping around him, pulling him in until his shoulder collides with a firm chest. Mydei holds tight, holds fast. “All this over some fake fucking cats. Stop talking.”

“It’s not the cats,” Phainon says, laughing wetly, chin wobbling, pressing his face into Mydei’s shoulder. “You shut up.”

△

A bit later, he watches Mydei line his eyes in red again. It’s unexpectedly satisfying, the way he does it in one smooth line. Such a mundane thing, and yet.

They make eye contact in the mirror. “Did you forget something in here?” Mydei asks, and Phainon gets this embarrassed kind of Deja Vu. Mydei’s bangs are clipped back again, and with only one eye done he looks exceptionally silly. He should look exceptionally silly, but Phainon is stuck looking, looking, looking. He always is. There’s a lump in his throat. It still hurts from crying.

“I wanted to watch,” he admits, excruciatingly attracted to the way Mydei’s gaze narrows, expression otherwise flat. “It’s like… those satisfying calligraphy videos.”

“...Calligraphy?” Mydei repeats, pausing briefly to give Phainon an odd look before he resumes, leaning toward the mirror and doing his other eye with just as much ease as the first.

“You make it look so easy,” Phainon says, fighting the warmth that crawls up his neck. “I have a sister, you know. I’m very familiar with her complaining when it comes to that sort of stuff.”

“My hands are steady,” Mydei says simply, straightening up when he’s finished, checking that his eyeliner is even. “And I have a lot of practice.”

He’s going to say something embarrassing again, his self-control stretched thin from his tears. He can feel it in the flip and tumble of his stomach, the heat in his face, but he can hardly stop the words from spilling out. “I really like it.”

Now, Mydei unclips his bangs, combs them out with his fingers. He meets Phainon’s eyes again in the mirror, says tonelessly, “Thanks.”

Phainon still looks like he’s been crying. He sniffs, rubbing his neck, tugging on his choker. “You’re welcome,” he tries, but it comes out all weird. Mydei turns to him, and the full force of his red-lined gaze hits. Phainon might throw up.

“One minute you’re all up in my space without a care in the world, the next you’re super fucking awkward,” Mydei says. “Are you embarrassed you cried? You already know I don’t give a shit about that.”

And here is it. Maybe he’s stupid, maybe he’s sentimental. Probably both. He wants a lot of things. Probably too many. He’s greedy and good at taking advantage, but Mydei always lets him. It’s Mydei, he thinks. When has he ever cared how greedy and dumb and embarrassing you are? Right now, he’s over the crying thing. Right now, he looks at Mydei and remembers what it feels like to want, what it feels like to have permission. “I’m not quite sure what I’m allowed, yet,” he says, hands tight on the doorframe.

Mydei crosses his arms, leaning against the counter like an invitation for Phainon to pin him against it. One of his eyebrows lifts. “So ask,” he says. “What am I going to do?”

“Ruthlessly make fun of me,” Phainon suggests, “and then say no.”

“Sounds like a normal day,” Mydei retorts. “What are you so scared of?”

It’s just Mydei, Phainon thinks again. He needs to stop being so afraid of things changing. They will and they are, and that’s inevitable. But… they’re still them, and not everything needs to end in disaster. He needs to remember that, make it stick. “You’re right,” Phainon says.

Mydei’s smile is all too smug. “I know.”

They’re already running late. They’ve wasted so much time this morning already, but Phainon is packed and ready, and a little longer can’t hurt. “I want to kiss you or something.”

“‘Or something?’” Mydei repeats.

Phainon exhales. It might be a laugh, it might be a sigh. “I want to kiss you,” he says again, surer. “And I know you already said it’s fine, but it feels weird to just go up and do it, so…”

“So you act all weird,” Mydei finishes for him.

Phainon frowns. “At least I asked, right?”

“Sure,” Mydei tells him, straightening up. He takes a step closer, two, raises his eyebrows when all Phainon can do is hold his breath and stare. “So what’re you afraid of?” he asks. “Scared you suck at it?”

“No!” Phainon says, and falters. “Well, wait, do I? No one’s ever complained, but—”

“Chronic fucking worrier,” Mydei breathes, sighing as he cups Phainon’s cheek. His hand is warm. Phainon cuts off. “You’re fine,” Mydei tells him. “You’re not bad at it, when you aren’t too busy smiling to reciprocate.”

“Oh.” He parts his lips, wets them, notices Mydei looking. “Well, then. You wanna?”

“Shut up,” Mydei says again, but he just sounds fond, and the next moment he’s crossing the last of the space between them and kissing Phainon properly. He makes it feel so easy, soft-mouthed, just a stamp of pressure, his fingers curling in Phainon’s hair. He’s there for maybe three seconds, and there’s a little wet sound as he pulls away, eyelashes kind of long as they flutter open in wake of his amber, red-lined gaze, and oh. Phainon’s eyes have been open this whole time. Based on his snort, Mydei can probably tell.

“Oh, no,” Phainon says when he notes how smug Mydei looks. “You don’t get to hold this over me. I’m going to be so fine and normal about kissing you in the future; you won’t even know what hit you.”

“Sure,” Mydei says, stepping back and absolutely laughing at him. “I look forward to it.”

△

Their last day of driving begins without incident. Mydei goes first, handsome and at ease at the wheel, and they make their way through midday traffic before they’re on the freeway drifting farther and farther away from the city. The longer they drive, the lighter the traffic gets, until they’re cruising comfortably with a handful of other cars forty minutes later. The sun is already high and hot overhead, the air conditioning is blasting, and Phainon is putting the fruits of a sleepless night’s research to the test.

“Hear me out,” he says, pausing the music as the end of the song he’d been playing fades out. His finger hovers over the next one he’d been planning on playing. “You’ve said no to everything else I’ve suggested, so I’m trying to speak your language here.”

Briefly, Mydei glances at him, noticing his phone in hand and scoffing. “Is this about me learning fingerstyle guitar again?” he asks.

“Yes,” Phainon confirms. “But this time, I’ve done research, so you can’t complain that I’ve picked something too hard. And, I’ve happened to choose something that I know for a fact that you’ll like.”

“When did you do research?” 

“I couldn’t sleep last night,” Phainon says. “I put an earbud in; you were fast asleep. Anyway.”

“Just play it,” Mydei tells him.

“Behold,” Phainon says in his car commercial voice. He hits play, and the absurdly long fingerstyle intro to this absurdly long song begins. Mydei recognizes it in an instant, if the quirk of his mouth is anything to go by. “Nothing Else Matters by Metallica, certified by the internet to be a good starting place for a beginner fingerstyle player; certified by my own suffering ears to be Mydei approved. What do you think?”

A sound halfway between sigh and laugh. “You’re really never letting this go, are you?”

“You sent me on this mission, Mydeimos,” Phainon reminds him. “Don’t be upset that I’m following through.”

“I’m not going to sing it.”

“That’s fine.” His mouth twitches. So close to a victory. He just wants to see Mydei excited the way he always is when he gives himself to something. That, and he’s hot when he’s playing the guitar, but Phainon won’t tell him that. “Even just learning the intro is enough for me.”

Mydei takes this deep breath, shakes his head. “Alright,” he says, a little long suffering, a little fond. “I’ll learn it.”

“Delightful,” Phainon says, smiling too wide. His phone buzzes in his hand atop his bouncing leg. He flips it over to see the screen. “It appears I’m receiving a call from my sister. You’ll have to excuse my cutting this short.” With a click, he accepts the call and shuts off the music, putting Cyrene on speaker.

“What convenient timing,” Mydei notes, “just as you turn on a song I like.”

Phainon can’t help but laugh. “Hi, Cyrene,” he says instead of responding.

“Hi,” she says. “I’m waiting to check out of the hospital now.”

“Shit, you’re unhooked and everything?”

“Unhooked and everything,” Cyrene confirms. A bit of shuffling on her end. “Stelle is here to take me home. We’re just waiting for the doctors to sign me out, which is taking forever, by the way. It’s already been forty minutes.”

“I wouldn’t be surprised if they leave you hanging for another hour,” Phainon laughs. “Prompt and timely healthcare in this day and age?”

“Ah, right, silly me,” she says, laughing too, and she might sound freer. Still tired, still sick, but a little better. Phainon can’t imagine spending a week cooped up in the hospital with nothing to do but sleep and feel sick. Going home is probably a light at the end of the tunnel. “Guess I’ll just wait another six hours.”

“You do that,” Phainon tells her. A glance at Mydei shows him listening with the edge of a smile on his face. He never has much to say, not on a call, not even when they’re visiting her in person, but it’s obvious that he cares. There’s something about that… having someone care about the things he does and act like it’s a given, as easy as breathing and as much of a no brainer as the sky and the sea being blue.

He’s lucky, isn’t he? Mydei is good at pretending he’s not, but he’s so good. Good to Phainon, good to everyone and everything he cares about. He’d probably hate it if Phainon called him out on that. It would probably piss him off if Phainon called himself lucky for having him, and Phainon loves him for that too.

He clears his throat, addressing Cyrene again. “How are you feeling?”

“Alright,” she answers. “Still pretty exhausted, and I’ve still got all the symptoms, but that’s normal. It’ll take a while for me to really feel better, and by then I’ll probably have to start treatment all over, but I’ll happily take fifty percent after a week of zero.”

“I hope you’ll feel better faster than that,” Phainon tells her, bouncing his leg and turning to look out the window in an attempt to not to get emotional again. He doesn’t need to cry twice in one day. He chews on the sores inside of his cheek, watches the sections of the traffic barrier blur together fast enough that his eyes struggle to focus.

“Me too,” Cyrene says. “Going home is enough for now, though. I can’t wait to sleep in my own bed and eat your leftovers and go outside.”

He exhales, and it’s like breathing out the weight of the world. “Oh, you’re in for a treat,” he says. “That cobbler Mydei made is amazing. Eat it fast before it goes bad, ‘cause my god…”

Mydei rolls his eyes. “It isn’t that special,” he says.

Phainon lets the corners of his mouth curl up. He feels good about this. Mydei by his side. Cyrene recovering, albeit slowly. He hadn’t been able to make sense of a lot of the doctor’s reports, but the count of abnormal cells in her blood is steadily coming down, and while the medication has been killing her healthy cells too, they’ve given her blood transfusions to make up the difference, and she should recover. Given time, her situation looks good, and that doesn’t make the now okay, but Phainon could swim in the relief.

Another exhale. Things are good, things are better. He gets to go home too. Sleep with his own blankets, eat Mydei’s cooking, not have to wake up just to drive for ten hours straight. Maybe that cry earlier was good for him.

He looks at Mydei, his profile, the cut of his jaw, his throat. His tattoos, the artful mess of his hair. What made him look at Phainon and decide he wants him? The more he thinks about it, the more absurd it gets. “We had the same cobbler, right?” he asks Mydei, who scoffs and presses his lips into a thin line. Pretending he doesn’t love the praise. God, if he knew how Phainon would drown him in it. “Don’t bother pretending to be humble.”

Cyrene’s laugh through the phone. “I can’t wait to try it,” she says. “I’ll fact check both of you, see who’s lying.”

“Mydei,” Phainon coughs, and reaches for his water. “Ah, excuse me, I think I got something caught in my throat there.”

Mydei offers his middle finger, and Phainon has to swallow quickly before he can risk spitting a mouthful of water as he laughs. “I hate you,” Mydei tells him, but he just laughs a little harder.

“Lying in front of my sister twice, Mydeimos?” he teasing. “You should be ashamed of yourself.”

This makes Cyrene laugh. Mydei told him once that she laughs the same as Phainon does. No matter how he was pressed, he wouldn’t explain what that meant. But her laugh is high and melodic and he misses her in a way that feels more sweet now than bitter. He takes another deep breath. Exhales it fully. “Are you gonna be okay, Cyrene?” he asks.

He can practically hear her smile. Imagines the way her eyes must soften. And then he remembers that his image of her isn’t quite correct anymore. She won’t have that pink hair. Her smile will be the same though, so it doesn’t make him sad to think about it.

“Yes,” she says. “I’m still sick, sure, but I’m getting better, and I’m not alone, remember?”

“Yeah,” he breathes.

“And I get to go home for the first time in a week! I get to go outside! Stelle and Dan Heng are going to be around, it’s fine, it’s good, so stop worrying.”

“It’s chronic,” Mydei and Phainon say at the same time, and Phainon laughs, laughs, laughs until he could cry again.

“But I’m glad,” he says when he’s gotten ahold of himself. “Remember the paperwork.”

“You’re worse than mom was,” Cyrene tells him. “I’m fresh off chemo and still half dead, let me breathe. It’s not like you’re even home yet to do anything with it.”

“But you will?” Phainon asks. She probably rolls her eyes, half a country away.

“Yes,” she says. “I will. And I’m gonna go since Stelle says the doctor is in the hallway. Bye, Phainon, Mydei.”

“Bye,” Phainon says back. “Keep us updated.”

“Bye,” Mydei echoes. He adds, a bit awkwardly, “Good luck with everything.”

“Thank you,” Cyrene says. “See you sometime.”

△

They switch once, Phainon driving after Mydei up until they decide to stop for lunch. They order sub sandwiches, wrapped in paper and easy enough to hold. When they sit down, Phainon bounces his leg and taps his fingernails so much on the table that Mydei asks if he wants to take a walk as they eat instead of sitting. He’s intimately familiar with every one of Phainon’s restless tells, and he figures almost five hours in a car is enough to drive anyone crazy, let alone someone who needs to move as much as he does.

“Is that fine?” Phainon asks. “I mean, I guess these wouldn’t be too hard to eat standing, but…”

Like walking around a bit is going to inconvenience Mydei in some way. He worries about the strangest things. Mydei was cooped up in that car too. He gets up instead of replying to that, just gathering his stuff and nodding his head. “Let’s go.”

Phainon bolts upright, grabbing his drink and his sandwich and tucking his chair in with his hip. Wordless, he follows as Mydei leads the way out.

It’s still hot, but it’s overcast and there are enough trees in the parkstrip to give them some shade as they head onto the sidewalk. Phainon sucks on his straw, fumbles with the paper on his sandwich before pausing. “What if we have a picnic,” he says. “It’s kind of nice out here, isn’t it? Plenty of lawn space and trees…”

“A bit late to set that up,” Mydei notes. “But if you want to get your ass wet sitting in the grass I won’t stop you.”

Phainon hums like he’s contemplating this. Their strides are in sync on the sidewalk. Phainon’s gray sneakers, Mydei’s black boots. Their footsteps sound the same. Phainon falls out of sync to avoid the cracks. “But will you join me in getting my ass wet in the grass?” he asks, looking at Mydei with this dumb smile. His eyes are so stupid blue, and his inner child has always been more of an outer child. Mydei likes that, for the most part. Phainon is fun, for all his impulsivity, and nothing he does is ever really bad. Maybe Mydei will get his ass wet, but it’ll dry, and Phainon will smile. He sighs, pretends to be tired of him. “Dead set on it, are you?”

“Would you rather sit on the sidewalk?” Phainon offers. Mydei laughs, shakes his head. It was one thing, stopping to pet a cat the day before. He can’t imagine just sitting down right here to eat their sandwiches. At least in the grass they’ll be out of the way.

“Yeah, fuck that,” he says, and waves ahead of them, to where they’re running out of trees. Six more, and then they’ll have to cross the street and walk in the sun. “Pick a tree. We’re sitting on dirty clothes if we get muddy.”

“It’s late enough that it’ll have evaporated if they watered in the morning, right?” Phainon asks, guiding them under the next one. It’s a slight incline, a dozen steps. They sit facing the street, businesses and parking lots behind them. Cars rush by, and admittedly, he’s right. The grass is fairly dry, though it’s prickly and Mydei has always had a very mild allergy. His pants will protect him, though, so he figures it’s fine.

The crinkle of paper as Phainon unwraps his sandwich. His sits cross-legged, his drink cradled between his legs to keep it stable. It’s funny how much calmer he seems, just sitting on the ground outside instead of at a table in the restaurant. He’s like this at home too; put him at a desk and he’ll fidget like he’ll die if he doesn’t. Put him on the floor and he’s as happy as can be. Until he starts complaining about back pain an hour later.

“See, this is pretty nice, isn’t it?” Phainon asks. “It’s cute out here.” Suburbs instead of the city or the middle of nowhere. Plenty of trees and green space, not too many people. The breeze whistles through the leaves. Phainon’s hair blows into his eyes.

“Sure,” Mydei offers, making the mistake of looking at him as he says it. Phainon smiles a little, close-mouthed and soft. Mydei turns away and takes a bite of his sub, watching the cars as he chews.

A buzz. Phainon wrestles his phone out of his pocket and checks it, smiling a little as he reads the text he’d gotten. “Cyrene says you’re a liar,” he tells Mydei, turning the phone so he can see it. His hand shakes, so Mydei reaches out to steady it. The cobbler is spectacular, and Mydei is a liar. Another text sends when he finishes reading the first. Mydei reads it and frowns. Also, he’s so disgustingly in love with you it makes him look stupid.

“Tell your sister she’s a bitch,” he says, and watches Phainon’s mouth drop open in offense.

“She didn’t even—” He pulls the phone back and reads the second text, which startles a laugh out of him and cuts off his words. “Oh,” he says, typing something back that he doesn’t let Mydei see. “She’s a delight.”

△

They get home late, as expected. The sky is already dark as they pull into Mydei’s parking space and slip out of the car to get their things. Phainon yawns as he drags his suitcase out of the trunk, the wheels clacking as he sets it on the asphalt. They’re lit with nothing but washed out streetlights. The sprinklers are on this late, watering the scant lawn around the apartment complex and puddling a bit on the sidewalk too. The soft hiss of them serves as their backdrop as Mydei grabs his duffle bag and the last of the snacks. Phainon gets the cooler, and then they’re struggling up three flights of stairs, leaving wet footprints as they pass through a puddle.

Phainon yawns again behind him as he unlocks the door, and as they slip inside, he sighs like it’s the greatest relief in the world. “Finally,” he says, kicking the door shut behind them as Mydei turns on the light. He drops the cooler in the kitchen and pushes his suitcase on its wheels in the direction of his room. “I can still hear the road.”

“Me too,” Mydei says, breathing in. It’s always strange coming back after a long time. It’s the only time he ever knows what home smells like. Old paint and laundry, or something like it. He heads to his room to drop off his bag and has to fight the urge to collapse into bed in his sweaty clothes. He’s so goddamn tired. It’s barely ten at night but he’s exhausted like it’s three in the morning. He needs a shower. He needs to not go to work tomorrow or the week after, just to recover from this.

The pipes start to groan. That loose washer screams through the walls as Phainon beats him to it. “That bastard,” he murmurs, squatting to unzip his bag and dump all his dirty laundry in his hamper. Better he does this now, because he’ll only procrastinate more and more if he waits. It only takes him a handful of minutes anyway.

He leaves his toiletries and something to change into on the bed to take to the bathroom when Phainon’s done, and then he sighs and drags himself to the kitchen to deal with the cooler. There isn’t much in there but a few leftover drinks, a single orange, and one last piece of the fruit cobbler he made wrapped in a plastic bag that must’ve gotten a hole in it, because there’s water inside and it’s all soggy from the melted ice in the cooler. He sighs and tosses it, then dumps the rest of the ice and water into the sink. He doesn’t touch the bag of snacks; he’ll leave that to Phainon when he comes out.

A handful of long minutes. The water finally stops running, the pipes stop groaning. Phainon comes out in his towel, probably having forgotten his clothes for the hundredth time. His bedroom door shuts behind him, and Mydei yawns into his hand before putting the last of his energy to this. A shower of his own before he takes a much needed rest.

The floor is wet. Phainon has dripped all over and didn’t bother to clean it up. He never does, but Mydei is much too tired to care. He showers in water near scalding, using his own soaps for the first time in what feels like ages. He brushes his teeth when he gets out, and when he finally lays down, uncaring of his wet hair, dressed in a pair of plain black sweats, it’s the best goddamn feeling in the world. He shuts his eyes and breathes just like that, then realizes he’ll have to get back up to turn off the light.

And then there’s Phainon in the doorway wearing green shorts and a loose, stained white shirt. He’s rubbing one of his eyes, dead on his feet.

“Hey,” he says.

“Turn off the light,” Mydei tells him, and he laughs but does, and they’re swathed in darkness. He can’t see a thing with his eyes unadjusted, but he can finally relax, and that might be the best goddamn feeling. The mattress dips and the sheets rustle as Phainon climbs in beside him.

“Scoot,” he says, bumping Mydei’s leg, and Mydei scoots. Phainon settles in next to him, warm and smelling like himself. He sighs softly, pulling on one of Mydei’s pillows. “Nice to be back, isn’t it?” he asks.

There’s nothing to see but dark, vague impressions here and there. Mydei closes his eyes, laying atop the covers, heavy with exhaustion. His breath is slow, even. “Mhm,” he manages. Phainon lets out this tiny laugh that bleeds into a yawn. Just the sound of it is contagious, and Mydei yawns too. “Let me under the blanket,” he grumbles, so together they shuffle around until they manage to wrestle it from underneath themselves. As it settles over his shoulders, Mydei changes his mind. This is the best goddamn feeling in the world.

Phainon’s foot brushes his shin. The sheets whisper as he slides closer, the blanket over him too, now. “Hey,” he whispers. His fingers curl lightly over Mydei’s wrist. They’re close enough to share air, face to face on their sides.

“Did you brush your teeth?” Mydei asks him, though his words kind of stumble and stick together.

“Yes,” Phainon answers, fingers tightening. “Would you…” A huff. He pulls on Mydei’s arm until he gets the memo, lifting it so Phainon can slide closer, his hand on Mydei’s bare back, head tucking under his chin. His hair tickles, cold and still damp from his shower, but the rest of him is so warm, and maybe it should be annoying that he’s here while Mydei is trying to fall asleep, but for some reason it’s nice instead. 

“Better?” Mydei mumbles. He knows how awkward it is to have to ask someone to hold you. He sets his hand on Phainon’s hip, up his side until it finds a comfortable spot belted around his waist.

“Yeah,” Phainon tells him. His fingertips swirl and skim and trace patterns on his spine, and that tickles too. Mydei shifts until he stops, and then they settle again. Pressed close in the dark, neither with much left to say. They’ve already spent the last week breathing each other’s air. Maybe they could talk about Cyrene or Phainon’s hometown and his family and whatever else has been bothering him, but it isn’t the right time for it. Right now is just for this. They’re too tired to bother with much else until morning anyway.

His cheek against Phainon’s wet hair. Careful, not trying to poke his eyes out in the dark, Mydei brushes Phainon’s bangs back, feeling carefully over the shell of his ear down his face. His hand is cold, out of the covers. The line of Phainon’s jaw is surprisingly sharp. He’s probably so stupidly, unfairly pretty. Mydei is so tired. “Are your eyes closed?” he asks.

“No,” Phainon says. “Well… They are now.”

“Keep them that way,” Mydei tells him, filled with this dumb feeling. With gentle fingers, he finds the corner of Phainon’s eye. He can feel his own heartbeat, pounding in his chest.

“What’re you doing?” Phainon breathes.

It would be easier to just fall asleep like this. To ignore whatever this feeling is, but Phainon… Mydei’s already established that he would go to the end of the country and back for him. He’d do so many things at the cost of so much, if only Phainon wanted it. He sucks in a careful breath and holds Phainon still as he kisses his eyes, each one in turn, so lightly it can hardly be considered a kiss at all. His eyelids flutter, and his eyelashes tickle a bit. It feels like he’s holding his breath.

When he’s done, Mydei settles back into his pillows, his hand on the back of Phainon’s head, tangled in his wet hair and guiding him close. “That was on your list, wasn’t it?” he murmurs. Phainon lets out something that might be a laugh, but it’s all air.

“Yeah,” he says, his forehead pressing into Mydei’s shoulder. “Yeah. It was.” He’s soft all over. Mydei doesn’t want to give him up to the world tomorrow. He knows he’s fine, that he isn’t hurting as much as he was, that he’s happy, but he still carries so much, and always will. Mydei can only hope he won’t make himself carry it all alone.

“Hey,” Phainon whispers. He pokes at Mydei’s ribs, and that tickles too until his hand goes flat. “Can I stay here tonight?”

“You’ve already made yourself at home,” Mydei points out, stifling another yawn. He runs his fingers through Phainon’s damp hair, tugging lightly on the ends.

“Maybe you’re sick of me,” Phainon says. His foot is shaking. “Maybe you were looking forward to finally having the bed to yourself.”

He wraps his arm firm around Phainon’s shoulders. “Shouldn’t you have asked before you climbed in if you were worried about that?”

“You let me,” Phainon whispers.

A grunt. “Do you think I wouldn’t kick you out if I wanted to?”

“Yeah, actually,” Phainon admits. “I do think that.”

Mydei makes an unhappy sound. Holds tighter in case he decides he wants to leave now. “Don’t grow a fucking ego,” he grumbles. “I would, and I will if you don’t shut up. You’re the one that struggles to sleep; why aren’t you excited to have the bed to yourself?”

Phainon laughs a little, his breath on Mydei’s throat. He’s so warm, palms sticky with sweat on Mydei’s back. Always so goddamn sweaty. His foot is still bouncing. “I guess I got used to having you by my side,” he says.

Mydei’s mouth against his temple. He traps Phainon’s foot under his own until it stills, though he knows he’ll just start moving something else in a handful of seconds instead. “Clingy,” he murmurs.

“Oh you want to talk about clinginess now, do you?” Phainon asks, prodding him again. He’s caught on to the fact that between the two of them, Mydei is the one with doglike loyalty.

“Just shut up,” he says, half asleep already. “Goodnight, Phainon. We have work tomorrow.”

“Don’t remind me.”

Mydei grunts back, shifting a little until he’s comfortable with the way they fit. “At least we’re home,” he murmurs, his arm around Phainon’s shoulders, Phainon’s around his waist. Their legs tangle. Phainon turns his ear to his chest. Hums, softly.

“I can hear your heartbeat,” he breathes.

Mydei blows on his hair, eyes stubbornly shut. “What am I even supposed to reply to that?”

A weak laugh. “I don’t know. It sounded romantic in my head.”

“Just go to sleep,” Mydei grumbles. They’re quiet for a breath, two.

“I love you,” Phainon tells him. Mydei’s too tired for his heart to flutter.

“Yeah, yeah,” he says into the pillow. “I love you too. Now shut up.”
